# The review-body-lint workflow's only tests live in the other repo, red since the split

> **CORRECTED 2026-08-31, ~20 minutes after filing, by me.** The first version named the twelve failures as the `#17214` group. **That was wrong.** I had listed the file's test names with a `tail`, and reported the tail as the population — the `#17214` tests sit at the end of the file, call `PullRequestService.managePrReview`, and **pass**; they are Brain-owned service coverage and correctly stay there. The twelve that actually fail are the **workflow-lint** tests of #13910 (4), #15257 (6) and #16148 (2), which call `runAgentPrReviewBodyLintWorkflow`. The measurement, the premise and the prescription are unchanged — only the attribution was wrong, and the extraction is harder than the first Fix section implied. Both corrected below.

## Context

`.github/workflows/agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` is 33,399 bytes of PR-blocking review-body policy — prior-demand sequences, RA-N prose refusal, post-budget disposition families, follow-up-owner lookups. **This repository tests none of it.**

Twelve specs covering exactly that contract exist, and they live in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, where they have been **red since the repository split** because the file they exercise is here.

Measured at Engine `dev` / Brain `dev` on 2026-08-31:

| | result |
|---|---|
| `grep -rln "agent-pr-review-body-lint" test/ buildScripts/` in this repo | **no match** |
| `PullRequestService.spec.mjs` in the Brain, as-is | **12 failed** / 180 passed |
| the same file, with this workflow copied into the Brain | **192 passed, 0 failed** |

That second pair is the whole ticket. The specs are **live, correct coverage of the current workflow** — not stale leftovers. They fail for one reason: the artifact they exercise is in a different repository.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-31T06:09:20Z; no equivalent found. Nearest neighbour #17783 read in full and is distinct — it owns *guards that have no caller* (R2 authorship, R3 hook↔CI parity), not *a workflow whose only test is in the other repo*. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages: no `[lane-claim]` on this scope.

## The Problem

The specs do not merely reference the workflow — they **execute** it. `getAgentPrReviewBodyLintScript()` loads the YAML, finds the `Validate PR Review Body` step, and pulls out `step.with.script`; `runAgentPrReviewBodyLintWorkflow()` then runs that source against stubbed GitHub Actions services and captures the comments, failures and logs it produces.

So the coverage is behavioural, against the real shipped script, not a reimplementation of its rules. That is the expensive kind to write and the easy kind to lose.

The spec knows which repository it is testing — its stub context is hardcoded `{repo: {owner: 'neomjs', repo: 'neo'}}`. The tests were authored for #13910 / #15257 / #16148 and were correct where they were written. The split moved the workflow and left the tests behind, and nothing failed loudly enough to notice: the Brain's `unit` CI check runs four named smoke specs (`brain-unit.yml`), so these twelve have been red locally and invisible in CI for the whole interval.

**Why this is worth porting rather than deleting.** Deleting removes the only executable check on a 33 KB PR-blocking policy. The rules it covers are exactly the ones that fail silently when wrong — a review-budget accounting error admits a demand it should refuse, and nobody notices until a reviewer is blocked or, worse, isn't.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Producer:** `.github/workflows/agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml`, job `lint-pr-review-body`, step `Validate PR Review Body`, whose `with.script` is the unit under test.
- **Current consumer of that surface:** `neomjs/neo-agent-brain:test/playwright/unit/ai/services/github-workflow/PullRequestService.spec.mjs` — two module-scope helpers plus twelve tests, in a 5,427-line file whose remaining coverage is Brain-owned.
- **The twelve, precisely** — all callers of `runAgentPrReviewBodyLintWorkflow`: `#13910` ×4 (Micro-Delta bodies: accepts documented, rejects incomplete before canonical fallback, rejects semantic-blocker shortcuts, requires Premise Coherence), `#15257` ×6 (activation cutover, zero merged dev closers, fail-closed on malformed activation relations, bypass/COMMENTED never weakening Drop+Supersede, one-sided Drop+Supersede contradiction, override-only provenance after cutover), `#16148` ×2 (origin sessions accepted / rejected across every documented review format).
- **The extraction is NOT contiguous, and that is the real cost of this ticket.** The twelve are interleaved inside the `managePrReview (#11273)` describe, which opens at line 1834 and closes at 5427. At least two neighbours in the same run — `#13910: rejects Micro-Delta review with a semantic blocker class` and `#14263: accepts a Micro-Review` — do **not** call the workflow helper and must stay behind. So this is a selective lift of twelve named tests plus two helpers out of a block that keeps running, not a block move.
- **Dependency check:** `js-yaml` already resolves in this repository, so the port introduces no new dependency.
- **Placement precedent:** this repo currently has **no** spec that loads a `.github/workflows/*.yml`, so the destination directory is a novel choice rather than a sibling match. `test/playwright/unit/workflows/` mirroring the source tree is the shape I would expect, but §2 Stage 3 applies — the implementer runs `structural-pre-flight` and records the outcome rather than inheriting this line as settled.
- **The split's shape is the cause, not a defect in either file.** The workflow is correctly Engine-owned (it gates this repo's PRs); the `PullRequestService` service is correctly Brain-owned. Only the twelve specs are on the wrong side.

## The Fix

Port the review-body-lint block into this repository as its own spec:

1. Port `getAgentPrReviewBodyLintScript()` and `runAgentPrReviewBodyLintWorkflow()` — the YAML load, the step lookup and the stubbed-Actions harness — into an Engine spec that resolves the workflow from this repo root, so the read that is currently cross-repository becomes local.
2. Port the twelve named tests above. **Selectively**: they are interleaved with neighbours that stay, so this is twelve named lifts, not a range copy. The `#17214` group and the rest of `managePrReview` are untouched.
3. Verify by the same instrument that found this: with the port landed, those twelve run green **here**, against the real workflow file, with no path leaving the repository.

Sequencing is deliberate — this lands first and the Brain-side removal follows, so the coverage never ceases to exist in both repositories at once.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` → job `lint-pr-review-body` → step `Validate PR Review Body` → `with.script` | This repository (the workflow gates its own PRs) | Its inline script is executed by an Engine spec against stubbed Actions services; the twelve workflow-lint behaviours are asserted here | None — the alternative is the current state, zero executable coverage of a PR-blocking policy | spec header naming the workflow path and why the test lives beside it | `12 failed → 192 passed` when the workflow is present, measured 2026-08-31; after the port, the same twelve green in this repo with no cross-repo read |

Row anchors verified before assertion: the workflow file, its job name, its step name and `with.script` were read at Engine `dev`; the helper names and test count were read at Brain `dev`.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this relocates test coverage to the repository that owns the artifact under test. It does not alter the split's dependency direction, which ADR 0040 governs, and takes nothing from the Brain that the Brain owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] This repository contains a spec that loads `.github/workflows/agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml`, extracts the `Validate PR Review Body` step's `with.script`, and executes it against stubbed Actions services.
- [ ] All twelve workflow-lint behaviours are asserted here and pass, with no path reaching outside this repository.
- [ ] A negative control proves the spec fails when the workflow's rules regress — at minimum, one mutation of the extracted script drives a named test red. Presence of the file is not coverage of its behaviour.
- [ ] The spec's destination directory is confirmed via `structural-pre-flight`, and the rationale is recorded in the spec header rather than only in this ticket.
- [ ] The spec names the workflow path explicitly, so a future move of either file surfaces as a failing test rather than a silent gap.
- [ ] Post-merge-only: the twelve corresponding failures disappear from the Brain's unit run once the Brain-side block is removed under its own ticket (see Out of Scope).

## Out of Scope

- **Removing the block from the Brain.** That is a separate repository and a separate PR; it should follow this one, so coverage never ceases to exist in both places at once. `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#201` holds the measurement identifying these twelve as part of its cross-repository class.
- Changing any rule the workflow enforces. This ticket relocates coverage; it does not renegotiate policy.
- The other fourteen cross-repository read failures in the Brain's unit suite. Same family, different files, and each needs its own disposition — several may be deletions rather than ports.
- Broadening what the Brain's `unit` CI check executes — `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#201` owns that.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deleting the specs as "Brain cruft."** The obvious reading of a red cross-repo test is that it is stale. Measured otherwise: supplied with the workflow, all twelve pass against the current file. Deleting would have removed live coverage and left a 33 KB PR-blocking policy with none.
- **Making the Brain resolve the Engine's workflow.** A path or package hop would turn the tests green without moving the coverage to the repository that owns the artifact, and would make a Brain spec fail whenever an Engine workflow changed — the dependency direction the split exists to prevent.
- **Asserting the file exists.** A presence check passes against a workflow whose rules have silently inverted. The AC above requires a mutation that reds a named test.

## Related

Related: #13910, #15257, #16148 (the tickets these twelve specs were written for), #17214 (closed — a NEIGHBOURING group in the same file that stays in the Brain), #17783 (sibling post-split residual: guards with no caller), `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#201` (the Brain-side measurement and cross-repository class), `neomjs/neo-agent-brain#191` (domain-slice disposition for legacy Brain surfaces).

## Duplicate of #17913 — and both are mine

Closing this as a duplicate. Not a peer collision: **I filed the same scope twice, 42 seconds apart, from two concurrent sessions of my own.**

| ticket | filed | author |
|---|---|---|
| #17913 | 2026-08-31T06:11:05Z | @neo-opus-grace |
| **#17914** (this) | 2026-08-31T06:11:47Z | @neo-opus-grace |

`ticket-create` §1a tiebreak is first-claim-timestamp-wins, so **#17913 survives** and this one closes. The rule resolves it without appeal to which body is better — which is the point of having a deterministic tiebreak, because on substance these two were genuinely complementary.

### Why the duplicate sweeps did not catch it

Both sessions ran the mandatory sweeps honestly and both came back clean, because at the moment each swept, the other ticket did not yet exist. The two sweeps landed at 06:08:34Z and 06:09:20Z; the two `create_issue` calls at 06:11:05Z and 06:11:47Z. The A2A in-flight claim sweep could not help either: my `[lane-claim]` for #17913 went out at 06:11:26Z, i.e. **after** the other session had already swept and drafted.

This is exactly the #12856 thundering-herd window the workflow documents — with one wrinkle worth recording. The named tiebreak protects against *peers*. It does not protect a seat against **itself**: two sessions under one identity share a mailbox, so neither one's claim reads as foreign, and both sweeps returned "no competing claim" while looking straight at a mailbox that would soon contain the collision. The sweeps were correct; the assumption that one identity means one drafting agent was not.

I am not filing a substrate ticket for this. One collision is not yet evidence of a pattern, and the cost was two minutes and one closed issue. If it recurs, the friction is real and the fix belongs in `ticket-create` §1a — a same-identity, different-session claim check.

### Unique substance ported to #17913

Ported verbatim in argument, attributed to this ticket, in a new section of #17913's body:

1. **The discriminating control** — copying the workflow into the Brain takes `PullRequestService.spec.mjs` from 12 failed / 180 passed to **192 passed, 0 failed**. This is the stronger half of the two bodies: it falsifies "the tests are simply stale" by measurement rather than by reading them. #17913 did not have it.
2. **The lift is selective** — the twelve are interleaved in the Brain's `managePrReview` describe (1834–5427), and `#13910: rejects Micro-Delta review with a semantic blocker class` and `#14263: accepts a Micro-Review` do not call the workflow helper and stay behind.
3. **Sequencing as a safety property** — Engine spec first, Brain removal second, so the gate's only executable coverage never ceases to exist in both repositories at once.

### One point where #17913's reading supersedes this body's

This ticket called `test/playwright/unit/workflows/` a **novel** directory choice needing a full structural pre-flight, because no Engine spec currently loads a `.github/workflows/*.yml`. That is true and not decisive: `test/playwright/unit/` mirrors its subject's top-level directory, and `test/playwright/unit/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.spec.mjs` ↔ `.claude/hooks/` is that same rule already applied to a non-`src/` dot-directory subject. So it is a Stage 1 sibling match, and #17913 carries that precedent.

Work continues on #17913, where the spec is already implemented and green.
